summary: Extends the Message-Context header from RFC 3458 with one more value, "video-message". A receiving mail client can use this as a hint to present the message in the best way.

plainLanguage.summary: A label on a package that says "video inside" so the person getting it knows right away how to open it.

subtitle: One new Message-Context value, video-message, so mail programs can tell a video email from other kinds.

tldr.problem: Email can carry video, but none of the Message-Context values from RFC 3458 properly identified a video message.
tldr.mechanism: This memo registers the value 'video-message' in the Internet Message Context Types repository, for messages whose primary content is video.
tldr.outcome: A receiving mail program may use the value as a hint for how to present the message. It requires no particular behaviour.

today: RFC 3938 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 3458. No later RFC obsoletes it.

sections.title: Message Context Background
sections.content: The Message-Context header from RFC 3458 tells a mail program what kind of message it has, which affects things such as which icon to show. RFC 3458 registered the contexts voice-message, fax-message, pager-message, multimedia-message, text-message and none.
sections.plainLanguage: Mail can have a label saying what is inside, like 'voice' or 'fax'. This document adds a label for video.

sections.title: Why Video Needs Its Own Value
sections.content:
Some email consists mostly of a video stream. The RFC gives examples of services connected to cell phones that capture video and video email services that use webcams on a PC. Such messages come in two flavours: the video is embedded in the message as a body part, or it is stored on a third party's video server.

Neither flavour is properly identified by an existing context, so the memo adds video-message.
sections.plainLanguage: Video can be inside the letter or kept at another place with a note pointing to it. Both need a 'video' label.

sections.title: The Registration
sections.content: The memo registers video-message in the "Internet Message Context Types" repository, as RFC 3458 specifies. The registered summary says it indicates a message whose primary content is a video mail message, usually recorded on a video camera, or whose main purpose is to hold an external reference to such a recording.
sections.plainLanguage: The new label goes into the official list of labels, with a short note about what it means.

sections.title: Only a Hint
sections.content: The header is intended to be an indicator of message context only. It is a hint and requires no behaviour on the part of a message user agent.
sections.plainLanguage: The label is just a helpful sticker. Nobody has to do anything special because of it.

references.text: Burger, E., Candell, E., Eliot, C., and G. Klyne, "Message Context for Internet Mail", RFC 3458, January 2003.
